text: Landing on water sounds soft. It isn't. At over two hundred kilometres an hour, water hits like concrete. If one wingtip or engine digs in first, the plane can spin round, and break apart. So a ditching needs four things. Wings perfectly level. The nose slightly up. The lowest possible speed. And the gentlest possible sink. And the Hudson offers something rare. A long, straight, calm stretch of water, with boats nearby.
